title: Tenant socket budgeter and progressive read-degrade for downstream resilience
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Problem: under cross-tenant load spikes and regional downstream degradation (Redis/Kafka/SQL), tenant requests compete for limited socket and connection capacity and cause SLO breaches for critical tenants. Current global connection governors are coarse-grained and induce noisy neighbour effects.

Goal: implement a per-tenant "socket budgeter" + progressive read-degrade policy that: (1) enforces soft per-tenant socket/stream budgets, (2) gracefully reduces semantics (full read -> read-only -> sampled read -> stale-cache fallback) per tenant when budgets are exceeded, and (3) integrates with existing circuit-breakers and multi-region failover so high-priority tenants maintain throughput during partial downstream outages. The feature should be observable, tunable, and reversible via rollout flags.
acceptance_criteria: Socket budgeter accepts config: tenant_budget (sockets), burst_multiplier, priority_tier
When global pool at 90% utilization, low-priority tenants enter progressive read-degrade path within 200ms of admission decision
High-priority tenants retain at least 70% of their baseline RPS under simulated half-region Redis degradation
No increase in median tail latencies for P0 tenants by >10% in canary region
Dashboard shows per-tenant socket usage, degrade state, and reason codes; alerts fire for >3% tenants degraded for 5+ min
Automated chaos job reproduces degrade transitions and verifies fallback correctness for Redis/Kafka/SQL
changes: 2026-02-12: Initial ticket created after postmortem of 2026-02-08 regional kv saturation incident; proposed socket-budgeter concept
2026-02-19: Architecture sync — chose admission-controller extensible hook vs sidecar approach; agreed on in-process admission controller for lower latency
2026-02-25: Prototype admission gate implemented in staging that samples low-priority tenants into 'sampled-read' pathway
2026-03-02: Design review feedback from PM & SRE: add explicit metrics and reason-codes, ensure RBAC for tuning budgets per customer; update docs
2026-03-06: Integration spike with circuit-breaker: on KB-store error-rate >5% ramp to read-only then stale-cache fallback; documented thresholds
2026-03-10: Canary rollout to eu-west-1 with 5% traffic for group:internal-alpha tenants; observed expected degrade state transitions and metric reports
runbook: Detect: alert fires when >0.5% tenants transition to degraded state in <60s; check per-tenant socket histogram
Mitigate: increase global pool cap (short-term), or adjust burst_multiplier for impacted tenant tiers
Rollback: disable socket-budgeter flag for region via feature-flag service
Post-incident: run chaos job and collect degrade-state traces and Redis/Kafka error logs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + integration tests against mock redis/kafka/sql
Phase 1 (staging): enable for internal test tenants only, smoke test with synthetic traffic
Phase 2 (canary): enable 5% traffic in eu-west-1 for non-critical customers, monitor SLOs for 48h
Phase 3 (gradual): increase canary to 25% and then 50% across two regions with automatic rollback on threshold breaches
Phase 4 (GA): enable per-tenant budgets for all regions and add UI controls in Console
notes: Trade-offs considered: sidecar vs in-process — sidecar isolates failures but adds network hop; in-process chosen for latency and simplicity
We avoid hard kills of connections; policy uses soft admission with gradual semantics change to preserve partial correctness
Owner-level tuning will be exposed in Console under 'Tenant Budgets' with audit logs for changes
Future work: integrate with token-banking for cross-region request borrowing and smarter hedging for long-running Kafka consumer backpressure
